api.flutter: TableCellSpec(child, align: TableAlign{start,end}, checkbox: bool) and TableRowSpec(cells, selected) / TableRowSpec.span(span, spanHeight) cover text-left/text-right alignment, the [&:has([role=checkbox])]:pr-0 checkbox-column padding drop, and the colSpan empty-state row.
api.web: TableHead/TableCell accept className overrides for text-right alignment and rely on the same [&:has([role=checkbox])]:pr-0 selector for checkbox columns; TableRow's data-[state=selected]:bg-muted maps to TableRowSpec.selected; a colSpan={columns.length} TableCell is the empty-state row Flutter's TableRowSpec.span reproduces.

states.flutter: _TableState tracks _hovered per row index and TweenAnimationBuilder<Color?> fades each _BodyCell's fill toward theme.muted.withValues(alpha: 0.5) on hover, theme.muted at full strength when TableRowSpec.selected — selection beats hover per _fill's own ordering.
states.web: TableRow: 'border-b transition-colors hover:bg-muted/50 has-aria-expanded:bg-muted/50 data-[state=selected]:bg-muted', with data-[state=selected] written after hover in source order so it wins at equal specificity — the same precedence _TableState.build documents.

disabled.flutter: Table/TableRowSpec/TableCellSpec expose no enabled/disabled field anywhere in the file — a table is a passive data display, not a control that can be disabled.
disabled.web: table.tsx's exported slots carry no disabled: variant on any element; a table has no on/off state of its own to disable.
disabled.note: Neither Flutter nor the web models a table as a control with a disabled state, which is the correct behaviour for a read-only data grid — nothing to compare.

interaction.flutter: MouseRegion(onExit) at the whole-table level plus a per-cell onEnter callback (_BodyCell.onEnter) drives the hover row highlight; there is no keyboard navigation model in the file — a table is not itself a tab stop.
interaction.web: TableRow's hover fill is pointer-only (hover:bg-muted/50); the native <table>/<tr>/<td> elements carry no built-in keyboard navigation either — any interactive content inside a cell (a button, a checkbox) is reached by ordinary Tab order through the DOM, not through the table structure.

semantics.flutter: table.dart wraps no Semantics node anywhere in the file — the flutter.Table's cells carry only DefaultTextStyle for their text content, with no table/row/columnHeader semantics roles applied to the structure at all.
semantics.web: The web renders a real <table>/<thead>/<tbody>/<tr>/<th>/<td> DOM structure, which every browser and screen reader already exposes with native table, row, columnheader and cell accessibility roles for free — no extra ARIA authoring required.
